title: fix: preserve stream usage across cost-only updates
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Keeps the latest token-count record when providers append cost/cache metadata without token totals.
- Still rejects missing counts and invalid later token-count records; never invents or merges usage.
- Leaves provider stream bytes unchanged. Runtime change: 12 lines in the existing validator.
- Tests byte preservation, invalid/missing usage, exactly one wallet debit, and one billed analytics event.

Validation: 40 focused tests pass; TypeScript and Biome pass. Separate from monitor error-message PR #14595.

gist.headline: The token ledger remembers
gist.blurb: Some providers send a final little cost note after the useful token counts. The stream now keeps the last complete count on hand, so one generation still gets one clean wallet debit and one analytics record.
gist.summary: The chat stream usage validator now preserves the latest valid token-count record when providers later append cost or cache metadata without token totals, while still rejecting missing or invalid token-count records.
gist.impact: Streaming generations retain accurate usage through provider-specific trailing metadata, producing exactly one wallet debit and one billed analytics event without altering provider stream bytes.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful librarian-accountant at a cozy retro terminal, placing a complete token ledger safely into a honeycomb filing slot while harmless trailing cost/cache notes drift past unchanged. A small CRT monitor robot can hold a stamped receipt marked "1x", with code-plants and flowers suggesting reliable data flow.
